tasks.short: Direct preventative maintenance on geothermal equipment

steps.what: Direct preventative maintenance on geothermal plant equipment and verify the work

tasks.design: The manager retains on-site maintenance direction and verification using existing work orders in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The design does not replace maintenance labour or plant safety decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment condition and safe work execution require local expertise.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing work-order access supports direction without removing it.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising abnormal conditions and coordinating safe work.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands plant conditions and can stop inappropriate work.

reach.learn: Equipment dependencies and safe work constraints

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: maintenance direction and verification remain human; no geothermal maintenance labour saving is established by the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is the manager's direction and verification, not technicians' execution or separate work-order scheduling.

Existing maintenance planners supply requirements and work orders; the manager checks actual conditions during s1. Technicians perform work after direction and provide completion information during s1 before verification; their unchanged labour earns no focal saving.
No structured safe-to-maintain flag is assumed. Use native work-order functions first; existing runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new application or maintenance process is introduced.
unknowns: Manager's hands-on versus supervisory maintenance duties
research_questions: How much focal maintenance time is direct observation rather than separate scheduling?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. No saving from unchanged maintenance execution or existing work-order runtime.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect geothermal plant and injection well operation

steps.what: Inspect geothermal plant or injection well fields to verify equipment operations

tasks.design: The manager inspects the plant and well field directly, comparing observations with existing readings in {OPS_SYSTEM}. An instrument reading does not replace inspection or establish proper operation automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaks, unusual sounds and site conditions may not be represented in existing telemetry.
tasks.enabler_now: Current readings provide context without removing the field visit.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting unexpected equipment behaviour in its physical setting.
tasks.human_edge: The manager recognises conflicting signs and escalates uncertain conditions.
tasks.altitude: Inspection responsibility and site presence stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate follow-up on abnormal equipment operation
reach.learn: Plant-specific failure modes and escalation routes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: physical inspection remains necessary in this design; no new sensor coverage or geothermal fault-detection capability is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the manager's inspection, excluding repair and separate routine operator rounds.

Existing instruments produce current readings under the unchanged operating process; the manager captures and interprets site observations during s1. No free structured condition assessment is assumed.
Test native trend access first. Existing sensor and system runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no sensing or inspection tool is added.
research_questions: Which inspection findings cannot be inferred from existing telemetry?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. The complete field inspection remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and manage geothermal operating budgets

steps.what: Develop geothermal budget assumptions and verify operational and cost inputs
Calculate geothermal operations budgets and actual-versus-budget comparisons
Manage budgets by investigating variances and approving the operating proposal

tasks.design: Configure native {ERP} budget calculations and saved comparisons from assumptions verified by the manager. The manager investigates variances and approves a versioned proposal; the system does not choose maintenance priorities or authorise spending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual consolidation and repeated arithmetic can sit between operational assumptions and budget review.
tasks.enabler_now: Native budget models can reuse agreed cost mappings and formulas.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing realistic assumptions and balancing plant reliability against cost.
tasks.human_edge: The manager interprets operational consequences of budget choices.
tasks.altitude: Less consolidation, with operational budget decisions retained.

reach.task: Compare maintenance and production budget trade-offs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native budget models can calculate fixed formulas from verified inputs; this task-specific budget saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is the manager's operating budget preparation and management, excluding payment execution and finance's final corporate authorisation.

Finance produces posted cost and commitment records under existing bookkeeping. In s1 the manager captures period, account/cost-centre mappings, currency, source versions, planned output, energy and maintenance quantities, unit costs and scenario formulas, checking missing values within the full 25% share.
Missing mappings or disputed assumptions return to manual calculation and s3 investigation. No free forecast, plant-readiness flag or automatically selected budget is assumed.

Test native ERP budget configuration first; existing automatic arithmetic earns no new labour saving. Seven extra focal hours cover assumption and model changes; 3 other-role hours count finance mapping maintenance.
unknowns: Existing budget tooling and hands-on consolidation time
Available production and maintenance cost detail
research_questions: Can the native model reproduce a manually checked budget and identify changed assumptions?

approvals.approved_version: Exact proposal, period, scenario assumptions, source versions and budget actions reviewed in s3; any change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+40=65, gross 35%, net 28% after 7 focal upkeep. Scenarios range from already automated budgets with no new gain through 21 points of consolidation removed minus 7 upkeep; input judgement and budget decisions remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and implement geothermal corrosion controls

steps.what: Select corrosion control or mitigation systems for the geothermal plant
Implement corrosion mitigation with technical specialists and verify operational effects

tasks.design: The manager reviews technical evidence in {DOCS}, selects the control approach and coordinates implementation with specialists. Operational observations in {OPS_SYSTEM} support verification without automatically selecting or changing plant controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Corrosion control depends on plant materials, chemistry and operating conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing technical records improve access to evidence but do not replace specialist judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing interactions and long-term performance under changing conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The manager reconciles specialist advice with actual plant operation.
tasks.altitude: Technical accountability and implementation coordination stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate specialist review of a materials-protection change
reach.learn: Corrosion evidence and plant change-control boundaries

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: corrosion-system selection and implementation require plant-specific engineering judgement; no digest capability establishes autonomous geothermal control.

assumptions: Boundary is managerial selection and implementation coordination, excluding laboratory analysis, specialist engineering and installation labour.

Existing plant staff and laboratories produce chemistry and condition evidence before s1. The manager selects the approach in s1; responsible technical authorities provide existing change authorisations after selection and before implementation in s2. Their unchanged work earns no focal saving.
Implementation staff generate observations during s2 before the manager verifies effects. No structured suitable-system or effective-control flag is assumed.
Use existing technical records first; native runtime earns no saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new automation is introduced.
unknowns: Plant chemistry, materials and change-control authority
research_questions: Which evidence currently governs selection and verification of corrosion controls?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+55=100; net 0%. Technical selection and on-site coordination retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Plant judgement and field work stay human; native budget arithmetic offers conditional clerical savings.
reach: Coordinate finance inputs and specialist technical evidence.
role.ambitious_version: Better grounded plant and budget decisions without claiming savings from physical or specialist work.
